text:
sasha: Quick Q — I'm triaging a spike in tail latency for a dedicated pool euw3-23 (pool-id: euw3-23). Where's the fastest place to check if this is saturation/backpressure vs a networking hiccup? Any quick queries or dashboards to point me to?

mike: Start with the Pool Overview dashboard -> Pools / euw3-23. Key panels: serve_latency_p99, active_workers, task_queue_depth. Short link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/pool-overview?var-pool=euw3-23

carla: For backpressure, focus on enqueue_latency and worker_steal_count panels. Also watch kvcache_evictions/sec — lots of evictions = wasted work. Loki quick: {job="inference", pool="euw3-23"} |~ "(enqueue|evict|steal)"

mike: PromQL to inspect queue depth briefly:
```
sum by(pool) (inference_task_queue_depth{pool="euw3-23"})
```
If queue_depth climbs while active_workers stays flat, you're hitting capacity.

platform-bot: [ALERT] POOL_HIGH_QUEUE triggered for euw3-23 at 2024-03-10T12:43:11Z — queue_depth=128 (threshold=100)

sasha: Thanks. If it is saturation, what's our quick mitigation? Can we bump capacity or fallback routing?

carla: Two quick mitigations: 1) Enable burst capacity in the Console (Pools -> euw3-23 -> Actions -> Allow burst +X%). 2) Apply a routing policy to send low-priority requests to a quantized cheaper model. Also check kvcache hit-rate — if it's low, consider warming or pinning prefixes. Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.example/display/OPS/Pool+Backpressure+Playbook

mike: For traces, look at Jaeger service inference-runtime, operation schedule_request. Long queue.wait spans point to scheduling/backpressure. Example Jaeger query: https://jaeger.redwood.example/search?service=inference-runtime&tags=pool%3Deuw3-23

sasha: Any quick alert tuning suggestions so this doesn't become noisy during deploys? The alert fired right when a rollout started.

carla: If deploys spike queues briefly, either add a suppress window during deploys or raise the alert threshold a tad. Current: queue_depth > 100 for 2m. Options: queue_depth > 130 for 5m, or suppress when tag service:deploy=true. You can also add a short cooldown (mute) tied to the deploy pipeline.

mike: Quick CLI to pull last hour of logs for the pool from Loki:
```
curl -G 'https://loki.redwood.example/loki/api/v1/query_range' --data-urlencode 'query={job="inference",pool="euw3-23"} |= "enqueue_latency"' --data-urlencode 'start=1707200000000000000' --data-urlencode 'end=1707203600000000000'
```
Swap timestamps for your window.

ops-oncall: If you need me to flip burst for euw3-23, ping me. If this persists >30m file an incident and tag SRE.

sasha: Perfect — I'll run the PromQL, check Jaeger spans and grab screenshots. Will update here with findings. Thanks all!
